questions.title: On-Campus Sectional Elimination Rules
questions.question: In the Accenture recruitment process, which of the following statements regarding the Cognitive and Technical Assessment is TRUE?
options: There is negative marking for unattempted questions.
Sectional cut-offs must be cleared in both Cognitive and Technical parts to unlock the Coding round.
The Coding assessment can be taken on a separate day at the student's convenience.
The Communication round has no impact on the final package or role allocation.
questions.correctAnswer: Sectional cut-offs must be cleared in both Cognitive and Technical parts to unlock the Coding round.
questions.explanation: Accenture employs a strict progressive elimination model. Only candidates who clear sectional benchmarks in Cognitive (Critical Thinking, English, Abstract Reasoning) and Technical (Pseudocode, Networking, Cloud, MS Office) immediately qualify for the Coding Round.

questions.title: Marking Scheme & Sectional Strategy
questions.question: What is the recommended time allocation strategy for the 90-minute Cognitive & Technical round?
options: Spend 60 minutes on Pseudocode alone and 30 minutes on the rest.
Allocate approximately 1 minute per question, maintaining a minimum 75% accuracy threshold across all sections.
Leave English comprehension until the final 5 minutes.
Attempt all questions randomly without reviewing answers.
questions.correctAnswer: Allocate approximately 1 minute per question, maintaining a minimum 75% accuracy threshold across all sections.
questions.explanation: With 90 questions in 90 minutes, time per question must not exceed 60 seconds. Since there is NO negative marking in recent drives, attempting 100% of questions with intelligent elimination gives the highest aggregate score.

questions.title: Superior Elements / Leaders in Array
questions.question: Given an integer array `arr` of size `N`, return all superior elements. An element is called superior if it is strictly greater than all elements to its right.
questions.explanation:
Optimal Python Solution:
```python
def find_superior_elements(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    if n == 0: return []
    max_from_right = arr[-1]
    result = [max_from_right]
    for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        if arr[i] > max_from_right:
            result.append(arr[i])
            max_from_right = arr[i]
    return result[::-1]
```
Time Complexity: O(N) | Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary.

questions.title: Time & Work Efficiency Question
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, while Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
LCM Method:
LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units (Total tank capacity)
Rate A = +60 / 12 = +5 units/hr
Rate B = +60 / 15 = +4 units/hr
Rate C = -60 / 20 = -3 units/hr
Net Rate = 5 + 4 - 3 = 6 units/hr
Time required = 60 / 6 = 10 hours.

questions.title: SQL Aggregate & Group By Logic
questions.question: Consider tables `Employees (id, name, dept_id, salary)`. Which query returns the second highest salary?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees);
SELECT salary FROM Employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2;
SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id;
questions.correctAnswer: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees);
questions.explanation: The subquery `(SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees)` finds the absolute maximum salary. The outer query finds the maximum salary strictly smaller than that maximum, which is guaranteed to be the 2nd highest salary even across duplicates.

questions.title: JavaScript Event Loop Output

2. Microtask queue (Promises) executes before Macrotask queue: '3'.

Output: 1, 4, 3, 2.

questions.title: Rat Food Distribution Problem
questions.question: A colony of `r` rats each needs `unit` amount of food. An array `arr` of size `n` represents the amount of food in each house. Return the minimum number of houses needed from left to right to feed all rats, or 0 if array is empty, or -1 if total food is insufficient.
questions.explanation:
Python Implementation:
```python
def solve_rat_food(r, unit, arr, n):
    if n == 0 or len(arr) == 0: return 0
    total_required = r * unit
    current_sum = 0
    for i in range(n):
        current_sum += arr[i]
        if current_sum >= total_required:
            return i + 1
    return -1
```
Time Complexity: O(N) | Space Complexity: O(1).

questions.title: Binary String Operations Parser
questions.question: Given a string `str` consisting of binary digits ('0', '1') and uppercase characters 'A' (AND), 'B' (OR), 'C' (XOR), evaluate the string from left to right and return the final single binary digit.
questions.explanation:
Python Solution:
```python
def evaluate_binary_string(s):
    if not s: return -1
    res = int(s[0])
    i = 1
    while i < len(s):
        op = s[i]
        val = int(s[i+1])
        if op == 'A': res = res & val
        elif op == 'B': res = res | val
        elif op == 'C': res = res ^ val
        i += 2
    return res
```

questions.title: Mock 2 Pseudocode Evaluation
questions.question:
What is printed by the following code?

Integer x, y
Set x = 15, y = 9
If ((x & y) > (x ^ y))
  Print x
Else
  Print y
End If
questions.explanation:
In binary:
x = 15 = 1111_2
y = 9  = 1001_2
(x & y) = 1111 & 1001 = 1001_2 = 9
(x ^ y) = 1111 ^ 1001 = 0110_2 = 6
Condition: (9 > 6) is TRUE! Wait: If condition is true, Print x (15)!
Wait: if x & y > x ^ y -> 9 > 6 -> True -> Prints x = 15.

Rule of Alligation:
(Quantity of cheaper) / (Quantity of dearer) = (Price of dearer - Mean price) / (Mean price - Price of cheaper)

questions.title: Spontaneous Speaking Prompt (STAR Framework)
questions.question: Prompt: 'Describe a challenging project you worked on under a tight deadline. How did you ensure successful delivery?'
options: Structured Response using STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result)
questions.explanation:
Recommended 45-second structure:
- Situation (10s): 'During my 3rd year mini-project, our 4-person team had two weeks to integrate a payment gateway...'
- Task (5s): 'I was responsible for debugging API endpoint responses...'
- Action (20s): 'I modularized the webhook handler, established automated error logs, and worked with the team to test edge cases...'
- Result (10s): 'We submitted two days ahead of deadline and achieved 100% test case pass rate.'
